prior_finding_review.r3-l1-a4-001: VALIDATED — Traced the interactor guard order myself (create_subscription_event.rb): conversion_duplicate_exists? runs before the 5-minute dedupe, but the dedupe alone blocks delivery 2 in the test as written. Delivery 2's event_params are byte-identical to delivery 1's row (event_type 'trial_converted_to_paid', from_plan nil, to_plan organization.plan, stripe_subscription_id, amount 4900) and both deliveries run milliseconds apart, so `.where(event_params).where('created_at >= ?', 5.minutes.ago).exists?` matches. With conversion_duplicate_exists? AND the partial index both deleted, the second delivery fails on the pre-existing dedupe, `change(SubscriptionEvent, :count).by(1)` and the CONVERSION_EVENT_TYPES count == 1 both still pass — the example cannot falsify the §3 invariant, and in production the dedupe does NOT enforce it (redeliveries >5 minutes apart would create duplicate conversion rows undetected). The proposed fix is sound: backdating the first row's created_at past 5 minutes (or travel) between deliveries makes the dedupe miss, leaving only the §3 machinery as the enforcing mechanism, so the test then fails when guard+index are deleted. Note the interactor spec's own uniqueness examples (create_subscription_event_spec.rb) do NOT share this defect: they use cross-type pairs (converted_to_paid row vs trial_converted_to_paid call), which the dedupe can never match (different event_type), and they assert the guard's distinct failure message ('Conversion SubscriptionEvent already exists...') vs the dedupe's ('Duplicate SubscriptionEvent created within the last 5 minutes'), pinning the mechanism.

findings.title: Ledger-failure isolation example: every assertion's enforcing mechanism in-test is the branch's PRE-EXISTING outer StandardError rescue tier, not the feature's own begin/rescue it exists to verify; the CreateSubscriptionEvent raising stub is stubbed-but-never-asserted (the run-1/run-2 class)
findings.detail: Same vacuity class as r3-l1-a4-001, in the other §9.1-load-bearing example. The example stubs `allow(CreateSubscriptionEvent).to receive(:call).and_raise(StandardError, 'ledger boom')` and asserts: no raise, stripe_current_period_end_at updated, stripe_update_default_payment_method received, reset_ai_credits received. All three existing-behavior calls execute BEFORE the insertion point (insertion is appended at the END of the else-branch), so a later raise can never un-happen them — those assertions pass regardless of any rescue. The `not_to raise_error` assertion is enforced in-test by the invoice.paid branch's pre-existing outer tiers (stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb ~336-346: `rescue Stripe::StripeError`, `rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid/RecordNotFound`, `rescue StandardError` — all log-and-swallow, no re-raise). Mental-deletion check per rule 26 with agent 4's lens: (a) delete ONLY the feature's own `rescue StandardError` inside the insertion → 'ledger boom' propagates to the outer 'UNEXPECTED error' tier, is swallowed, every assertion passes — the exact mechanism the example exists to verify (§5.2's rescue isolation, D6 'individually rescue-wrapped') is gone and the test stays green; (b) delete the ENTIRE insertion → the raising stub is never invoked (RSpec `allow` requires no invocation), every assertion passes. No assertion ties the example to the feature: no `expect(CreateSubscriptionEvent).to have_received(:call)`, no assertion on the ledger-specific rescue's log line. This is simultaneously the run-1/run-2 defect class (stubbed-but-never-asserted) — the same class already fixed twice in THIS example's sibling assertions (7574df408 reset_ai_credits, e850c74fe sync_with_stripe) — now on the example's central stub. Borderline rule-26 ghost (assertions pass under whole-feature deletion); filed HIGH for consistency with the run-1/run-2 and r3-l1-a4-001 classifications since the example does exercise real feature code when the feature is present — orchestrator may escalate.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the feature's own rescue the enforcing mechanism: (1) add `expect(CreateSubscriptionEvent).to have_received(:call)` so deleting the insertion fails the example; (2) spy the logger (`allow(Rails.logger).to receive(:error).and_call_original`) and assert `expect(Rails.logger).to have_received(:error).with(/invoice\.paid SubscriptionEvent ledger error/)` — deleting the own-rescue then fails the example because the outer tier logs 'UNEXPECTED error' instead. Optionally also `expect(Rails.logger).not_to have_received(:error).with(/UNEXPECTED error/)` to pin 'never reaches the existing rescue tiers' directly. Secondary note (not filed separately — §9.1's failure clause enumerates only the invoice.paid behaviors): no failure-isolation example exists for insertion 2 (subscription.deleted), whose own rescue (§5.3) is equally untested; if the fix agent adds one, it must carry the same log-message assertion or it will be vacuous the same way via the deleted-branch's outer swallow-tier (stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb ~228-231).
